note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: ICR Score and ICR Probe: from dynamic hidden-state motivation to detection results

nodes.name: Static hidden states limit detection
nodes.description: Existing hidden-state hallucination detectors focus on static, isolated, high-dimensional (~4000-d) representations, which limits feature extraction and fails to capture hidden-state updates and cross-layer residual stream evolution.

nodes.name: Module roles differ
nodes.description: MHSA redistributes existing contextual information through query-key affinity, whereas FFNs act as key-value memories that retrieve and inject parametric knowledge; their contributions to hidden-state updates vary across layers.

nodes.name: Ratio of contributions unreliable
nodes.description: Directly taking the ratio of the attention and FFN contributions to the residual update is unreliable, because the FFN output is computed from the attention output.

nodes.name: ICR Score definition
nodes.description: The ICR Score is the Jensen-Shannon divergence between the softmax-normalized projection of the hidden-state update onto context token states and the head-averaged attention scores (top-k tokens by attention); small values mean attention-driven updates and large values mean FFN-dominated updates.

nodes.name: ICR layer-wise pattern
nodes.description: Mean ICR scores follow a stable layer pattern: low in early layers (0-3, MHSA-driven), rising and peaking around layers 10-15 (FFN-driven parametric knowledge integration), then declining after layer 21; the pattern is consistent across four datasets with narrow variance bands.

nodes.name: ICR separates hallucinations
nodes.description: Using the ICR score directly as a classification feature on HaluEval, AUROC exceeds 0.7 in ten layers and peaks at 0.7690 at layer 11, with clear density separation between hallucinated and non-hallucinated samples.

nodes.name: ICR Probe design
nodes.description: Because one layer gives only a partial view, the ICR Probe is an MLP (L,128,64,32,1) trained with binary cross-entropy and Adam on the token-averaged 1xL ICR vector across all layers, outputting the probability of a non-hallucinated generation, with under 16K parameters for L<42.

nodes.name: ICR Probe outperforms baselines
nodes.description: On Gemma-2, Qwen2.5 and Llama-3 across HaluEval, SQuAD, HotpotQA and TriviaQA, the ICR Probe outperforms training-free (PPL, LN-Entropy, LLM-check) and training-based (SAPLMA, SEP) baselines on most datasets (e.g. Gemma-2 HaluEval AUROC 0.8436 vs SAPLMA 0.8101).

nodes.name: Efficient single-pass detection
nodes.description: The ICR Probe uses only ~16K parameters versus 110K for SAPLMA, needs no layer or token selection, and detects hallucination from a single generation without multiple samples.

nodes.name: Better cross-dataset generalization
nodes.description: Trained on one dataset and tested on another, the ICR Probe keeps AUROC >= 0.66 and outperforms SAPLMA and SEP, with an average in-domain to cross-domain AUROC drop of 8.61% versus 10.18% (SAPLMA) and 11.67% (SEP), attributed to modeling intrinsic residual-stream dynamics.

nodes.name: Both ICR components matter
nodes.description: Ablation on Gemma-2: with neither hidden-state projection nor attention AUROC is 0.5; the projection alone gives AUROC 0.7723-0.7993; combining projection and attention gives the best results (e.g. HaluEval 0.8436), so the components are complementary.

nodes.name: Middle layers are critical
nodes.description: Removing the middle layers (15-28) reduces AUROC more than removing early or deep layers on most datasets (e.g. HaluEval 0.7774 vs 0.8436 full), showing their critical role in detection.

nodes.name: Token-level detection works for key tokens
nodes.description: Applied per token, the probe assigns low probabilities to key answer tokens in hallucinations (e.g. 'hectares' 0.04, ' Vietnam' 0.19) but unreliably handles frequent uninformative tokens like 'The' (0.98) and '.', so it mainly captures residual-stream patterns of key tokens.

isolated_nodes.name: Evaluation setup
isolated_nodes.description: ICR Probe is evaluated on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B-it using AUROC on HaluEval, SQuAD, TriviaQA and HotpotQA.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from the limitation of static hidden-state detectors and module-role background, through the ICR Score and its empirical properties, to the ICR Probe, its results, generalization, and ablation/interpretability analyses.
